scope: Independent engineering review of all24calledpasses in frozen manifest order, using saved all-22 trajectories, native events and full existing telemetry. No simulation, outcome filtering or engine modification. Four six-play all-22 path sheets aided review.
interpretation: Two mesh sequences lose useful arrival/support, one with actual pre-catch teammate collision. They nominate a coordination/request-boundary diagnostic; they do not prove a universal flight, pursuit or contact defect. Other completions, drops, a PBU, sacks, scrambles, contact escapes and supported finishes remain legitimate evidence. Secondary belief and escape nominations are not added to primary bad-football incidence.
limits: Balanced panel incidence is not game-wide prevalence; onlyfour frozen matchups andone fixedseed perconcept.

Native recorded positions/facing are already quantized to0.1 in PlaySim.recordFrame; existing fulltelemetry velocities/intents are quantized to0.01. Raw outputs preserve those native values; initial/final bodies retain greater precision. Use stored velocities, not finite-difference speeds or exact sub-tick geometry.
Frame times label enclosingtick afterphysics. Original event times retained; a same-tick order is not independent continuous timing.
Final intents include contact/spacing refinements. Actual perception calls are acquired inputs, not proof a particular behavior consumed them causally.
Sampled contacts are not a complete impulse ledger. Actual contact, bond/grip and support state do not establish real-world force or grip realism.
An original/expected target is distinct from the actual catcher; A008 explicitlypreserves H→Y incidental reception.
Repeated Cover4→Cover2 posterior mismatch is a secondary family-recognition question with no established harmful decision. Failed scramble endpoints likewise do not establish a feasible alternative.
